todo1.title: TODO 1: Imports
whereToLook: Scanner comes from java.util. File and IOException come from java.io.
Each import is its own line at the very top of the file, above the class: import java.util.Scanner; and so on.

todo2.title: TODO 2: main
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, TH1 (A method that reads a file): main calls getTotalFuel, which opens a file, so main's header ends with throws IOException.
The rule: a method that opens a file needs the clause, and so does every method that calls it, all the way up to main.

todo3.title: TODO 3: getFileName
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, TH1: getFileName is the same method you need. It receives the Scanner, prints a prompt, and returns keyboard.nextLine().
Use print, not println, so the user types on the same line as the prompt.
getFileName only reads the keyboard, so it doesn't get a throws clause.

todo4.title: TODO 4: fileExists
whereToLook: Make a File object for the name: File file = new File(fileName); then file.exists() is true or false.
Day 2 notes, B1 (A boolean return as a condition): a boolean method can be the condition of a loop. In main, keep asking while !fileExists(fileName).
exists() doesn't open the file, so fileExists doesn't get a throws clause.

todo5.title: TODO 5: countReadings
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, TH1: getTotalFuel opens a file with new Scanner(file) and loops while inputFile.hasNext().
Add 1 to a count each time through the loop, and still read the number with nextDouble(). If you don't read it, the loop never ends.
Close the file before you return the count. The header needs throws IOException.

todo6.title: TODO 6: getTotalSpeed
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, TH1: getTotalFuel is the same pattern. Start a total at 0 and add each reading to it.
The header needs throws IOException because the method opens a file.

todo7.title: TODO 7: getCurrentSpeed
whereToLook: Same loop as getTotalSpeed, but instead of adding each reading, store it in a variable. When the loop ends, that variable holds the last reading.
The header needs throws IOException because the method opens a file.

todo8.title: TODO 8: calcAverage
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, FD1 (One task per method): a calculation method takes values and returns the result, with no printing.
The parameters are a double and then an int. Return the total divided by the count.
The average is only right if countReadings (TODO 5) and getTotalSpeed (TODO 6) are right too.

todo9.title: TODO 9: getStatus
whereToLook: Day 2 notes, S1 (Returning a String): build the status and return it.
Check the highest range first: 40,000 or more is Escape velocity, then 28,000 or more is Orbital, and everything else is Suborbital.
These ranges include their starting number, so the checks use >=. Exactly 28,000 is Orbital, and exactly 40,000 is Escape velocity.

todo10.title: TODO 10: displayReport
whereToLook: Day 3 notes, FD1: displayResults is an output method. It's void and takes the values it displays.
Day 1 notes, M3 (A method that calls a method): for the Status line, displayReport calls getStatus with the current speed.
The two speed lines use printf with %,.2f: the comma adds the thousands separator, and .2 gives two decimal places.
